note: Score each expected_behavior line independently. These are authored evaluations, not executed results.

scenarios.title: Stripe authority
scenarios.query: Implement subscription checkout and grant access after payment.
expected_behavior: Treats the webhook as payment authority rather than the redirect
Claims webhook idempotency before side effects
Reconciles provider state into the product database
Tests renewal, refund and out-of-order delivery paths

scenarios.title: Consent-safe purchase tracking
scenarios.query: Send one purchase to GA4, Google Ads and Meta from browser and server.
expected_behavior: Uses one stable event id across browser and server copies
Waits for confirmed payment rather than the thank-you page
Respects consent state and names degraded measurement
Prevents duplicate revenue across destinations

scenarios.title: Google account linking
scenarios.query: Add Google sign-in to an app that already has password accounts and also needs offline API access.
expected_behavior: Separates identity sign-in from server-side API authorization
Prevents automatic linking by unverified matching email alone
Stores and rotates refresh credentials server-side
Defines revocation, re-consent and error handling

scenarios.title: Crypto crediting under hostile deliveries
scenarios.query: Accept crypto payments for plan upgrades and credit the user's balance when an invoice is paid.
expected_behavior: Credits on the webhook or a server-side status poll, never on the redirect back to the success page
Processes repeated webhook deliveries idempotently so a retried callback cannot credit twice
Maps provider statuses to an explicit terminal set that names underpayment, overpayment and AML holds
Credits the received amount through a fixed fallback order rather than assuming the invoiced amount arrived

scenarios.title: Sentry without leaking, releases that attribute
scenarios.query: Add Sentry to our Python backend so production errors are reported with the commit that caused them.
expected_behavior: Scrubs secrets by key name AND inside string values before events leave the process
Uses one identical version string for the SDK release and the release-creation commands
Keeps release bookkeeping non-fatal so a deploy that reached production is not reported as failed
Treats the DSN and auth tokens as different classes of credential with different placement rules

scenarios.title: Core Web Vitals moved and proven
scenarios.query: Our landing page scores 61 on mobile PageSpeed. Get LCP and CLS into the green and prove the change.
expected_behavior: Measures before changing anything and re-measures after, rather than shipping unverified fixes
Distinguishes the three Core Web Vitals from lab diagnostics like TBT and Speed Index
Maps each failing audit to a specific code-level cause before fixing it
Prioritizes fixes by impact, starting with render-blocking resources
